name: Lucena position
principle: Rook + pawn on the 7th with your king in front: shield the king with the rook (build a bridge).
plan: Check the enemy king one file further away, then bring the rook to the 4th rank so it can block the checks.

name: Philidor defence
principle: Defending rook + pawn: keep your rook on your 3rd rank until the pawn advances, then check from behind.
plan: Keep the rook on b6 (stopping Kf6); after e6, go to the 1st rank and give checks from behind.

name: Opposition
principle: King + pawn vs king: the attacker must reach a key square two ranks in front of the pawn; the defender keeps the opposition.
plan: Defender: answer every king move by standing opposite it with one square between; attacker: reach d6, e6 or f6.

name: Rule of the square
principle: A king catches a passed pawn only if it can step into the pawn's square (the square from the pawn to its queening rank).
plan: Count: Ke2 enters the a5-e1 square and catches the pawn; one move slower and it queens.

name: Outside passed pawn
principle: An outside passed pawn decoys the enemy king; then your king eats the pawns on the other wing.
plan: Push the a-pawn to pull the black king to the queenside, then invade on the kingside with Ke4-f5 or d5.

name: Rook behind the passed pawn
principle: Rooks belong behind passed pawns, yours and the opponent's; a rook in front of the pawn is passive.
plan: Keep Ra1 behind the a-pawn and push it; Black's rook on a8 is tied down while your king walks up.

name: Wrong-colored bishop
principle: Bishop + rook pawn only wins if the bishop controls the queening square; otherwise a king in the corner draws.
plan: Stronger side: don't trade into this; weaker side: run the king to h8 and never leave the corner.

name: Pawn race
principle: In a pawn race, count the moves to queen for both pawns, who moves first, and whether the new queen gives check.
plan: h4 needs 4 moves, a4 needs 3: Black queens first, so White must bring the king or find a check instead.

name: Don't trade into a lost pawn ending
principle: With fewer pawns, keep the rooks on: rook endings are drawish, but a pawn ending a pawn down is usually lost.
plan: White should not play Rxd8 Kxd8; keep the rooks (e.g. Rc1, then Rc7) and attack the a-pawn.

name: Queen vs pawn on the 7th
principle: Queen vs pawn on the 7th: check or pin until the king must stand in front of the pawn, then bring your king one step closer.
plan: Repeat: force the king to d1 with checks, use that tempo for Kb2-c3 style king moves; c-, f- and rook pawns can draw by stalemate.
